reason: The hunk shows the test retained as commented-out code, not simply removed.
The signature improves parameter visibility, but the excerpt does not show new types or a type-checking change.
The inserted path misspells community, so the excerpt does not show a valid table-of-contents link to the intended page.
The removed escape is redundant for a literal space in this pattern, so the hunk does not change which links split.
The blank line is shown, but the title and excerpt give no reason for adding it.
The manifest directive names the three files, but the excerpt does not show which build consumes docs/MANIFEST.in or verify the final distribution contents.
The new contributor is shown, but the excerpt does not establish that the AUTHORS file covers all contributors.
The comment identifies a misspelling as one possibility for LookupError and gives no evidence of how often this is the cause.
The setting allows prerelease interpreters in the test setup and does not govern package dependency installation.
The checkout switches to the release branch, but the build edit does not pin or demonstrate a stable released version.
The new behavior deliberately raises an exception when a scheme is absent, so missing schemes do produce an error.
The badge image URL now encodes a space, but the excerpt does not show that it was failing or that the updated image loads.
The README feature list is shown, but the excerpt ends before sessions.py and does not establish that it implements the listed capabilities.
The edit exposes a read-only interface to type checkers but does not make the runtime headers data immutable.
The blank line is added, rather than deleted.
The wrapper changes the copy but still passes the original kwargs, so return_response=False is not forwarded through the copy.
The new condition selects when to look up certificate verification settings in the environment, without itself enabling SSL verification.
The deleted UnicodeError and TypeError handler is shown, but the excerpt lacks the fallback path needed to verify that it previously returned an empty string.
The new argument affects proxy bypass checks and environment proxy resolution, while explicit proxy entries are copied into the result.
Skipping a file value of None is analogous to omitting that query parameter, but in JSON an object value of None serializes as null.
The old call disabled preloading in every case, and the new call makes preloading follow do_block. It does not set a block argument.
The diff changes the documentation field spelling, but it provides no rendered output or identified rendering failure.
The image is indented, while its alignment attribute and URL remain identical. The new alignment result is unsupported.
The code encodes the entire network location rather than extracting and encoding only the hostname.
The excerpt shows the public module's import being removed but does not establish that it was unused or unreachable to callers.
The cleanup call changes, but the excerpt does not identify a resource leak or show that connection exhaustion is prevented.
The explicit parameter and forwarding are shown, but the excerpt does not identify a prior query handling issue beyond the signature difference.
The change deliberately delegates content reads to the file object after removing the response's read alias, rather than introducing a typo.
The cache is removed, but the excerpt does not identify a memory issue and the previous cache was already capped at 1,000 entries.
The edits revise the introduction, but the excerpt does not support a searchability benefit.
The test verifies the number of history entries and final status, but does not inspect their contents or order.
Both bounds are exclusive, so the new requirement does not permit version 2.9.
The action revision and version are clear, but the excerpt does not establish that it provides the latest features and fixes.
The attribution is added separately and the support call-to-action stays in the sidebar with a shorter heading.
The conversion removes dependence on local timezone settings where Requests runs, rather than changing how it handles the remote server's timezone.
